experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at the iconic Magic Kingdom, home to Cinderella Castle, Space Mountain, and the beloved Festival of Fantasy parade. Arrive at rope drop (park opening) to maximize ride time before crowds build. With a late flight arrival on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 onward. Stay at a Disney on-site hotel like Disney's Contemporary Resort or Disney's Polynesian Village Resort — both are within walking distance or a short monorail ride to Magic Kingdom, eliminating transit time and letting you return for afternoon naps before evening fireworks.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore EPCOT's World Showcase, a living cultural and culinary journey through 11 countries including Mexico, Japan, France, and Morocco. Sample authentic dishes, watch live cultural performances, and browse artisan crafts. This is ideal for families who want entertainment and education combined. Stay at Disney's BoardWalk Inn or Disney's Beach Club Resort — both are within a short walk or boat ride to EPCOT's International Gateway entrance, saving significant travel time each day.
experiences.location: EPCOT, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios & Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the fully realized world of Star Wars at Galaxy's Edge, where you can pilot the Millennium Falcon, build a custom lightsaber, and encounter stormtroopers. Also enjoy Toy Story Land and the thrilling Tower of Terror. Book Lightning Lane passes in advance for top attractions. Disney's Art of Animation Resort and Disney's Pop Century Resort are directly connected to Hollywood Studios via the Disney Skyliner gondola system — a fun, fast, and free transit option that kids love.
experiences.location: Hollywood Studios, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed evening at Disney Springs, Disney's free-admission shopping, dining, and entertainment district. Enjoy dinner at The BOATHOUSE or Rainforest Cafe, catch a live street performance, and browse Disney merchandise and unique shops. This is a perfect low-cost activity for Day 1 since your flight arrives after 20:00 — Disney Springs stays open until 11:00 PM and requires no park ticket. It's a great way to ease into the Disney experience without wasting a full park day.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Expedition & Pandora Experience
experiences.description: Explore Disney's Animal Kingdom, featuring the breathtaking Pandora – The World of Avatar with the Flight of Passage ride, a thrilling safari through Kilimanjaro Safaris, and live shows like Festival of the Lion King. This park is best experienced starting at morning rope drop when animals are most active. Disney's All-Star Resorts and Disney's Coronado Springs Resort offer affordable on-site stays with direct Disney bus service to Animal Kingdom, keeping your family close to the action throughout the week.
experiences.location: Animal Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Disney World, Orlando, Florida
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

day_by_day.morning: No activities - flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities - flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 via United Airlines. Collect luggage, take the free hotel shuttle from the airport to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and review your Disney World park tickets and plans for the week. Download the My Disney Experience app if not already done.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport food before departure
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport terminal food
meals.dinner: Grab a quick late-night bite at a 24-hour McDonald's or Denny's near the hotel on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (within 1 mile of hotel) — budget around $8–$12 per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep energy light tonight — big days ahead. Pick up snacks and water bottles at a nearby Walmart Supercenter (3.5 miles away on W Irlo Bronson) to save money on park drinks throughout the week. Set alarms early for Day 2. Confirm free shuttle schedule to Magic Kingdom at the hotel front desk.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take the free hotel shuttle to Magic Kingdom — aim to arrive at park opening (typically 9:00 AM). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain and Buzz Lightyear's Space Ranger Spin before crowds build. Then walk through Fantasyland to ride Seven Dwarfs Mine Train and Peter Pan's Flight using Lightning Lane if budget allows, or queue early. Explore Cinderella Castle and grab a photo.
day_by_day.afternoon: After lunch, head to Adventureland for Pirates of the Caribbean and the Jungle Cruise. Visit Liberty Square for the Haunted Mansion. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel (use the free shuttle) to rest and cool off — this saves money on park food and avoids peak heat and crowds from 2–4 PM.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom via shuttle for the evening. Enjoy Frontierland's Big Thunder Mountain Railroad and watch the spectacular Magic Kingdom Fireworks (Happily Ever After) at park close. Soak in the Main Street USA atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat breakfast at the hotel or use snacks purchased from Walmart — granola bars, fruit, and juice to save $10–$15 per person
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — budget-friendly counter service with fish and chips or chicken strips around $12–$15 per person
meals.dinner: Pecos Bill Tall Tale Inn & Cafe in Frontierland — hearty burgers and nachos around $13–$16 per person; use the free toppings bar to bulk up your meal

day_by_day.notes: Bring refillable water bottles — free ice water is available at any quick-service location. Wear comfortable shoes and apply sunscreen. June weather in Orlando is hot and humid (90°F+) with afternoon thunderstorms likely — pack a small poncho. Purchase a Disney Dining Plan or use mobile order on the app to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to EPCOT, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Head immediately to World Discovery for Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue — join as soon as the park opens via the app). Then ride Test Track and Mission: SPACE (Green Mission for a family-friendly option). Explore the stunning EPCOT Geodesphere and Spaceship Earth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through World Showcase — explore the pavilions of Mexico, Norway (ride Frozen Ever After!), China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Enjoy free cultural entertainment, street performers, and architecture. This is a great low-cost way to 'travel the world' without spending extra.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's nighttime spectacular — Luminous The Symphony of Us — a stunning fireworks and water show over World Showcase Lagoon. Free with park admission and a magical end to the day.

meals.breakfast: Hotel snacks or granola bars from Walmart stash
meals.lunch: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — one of EPCOT's best budget counter-service spots with rotating seasonal dishes, sandwiches, and grain bowls around $12–$14 per person
meals.dinner: Yorkshire County Fish Shop in the UK Pavilion — fish and chips for around $10–$13 per person, one of EPCOT's most affordable and delicious quick-service options

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is very walkable but large — wear comfortable shoes. The World Showcase doesn't open until 11:00 AM, so plan Future World/World Discovery first. Many World Showcase pavilions offer free entertainment and cultural experiences. Avoid expensive sit-down restaurants in World Showcase — they can run $40–$80 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Hollywood Studios, arriving at rope drop (typically 9:00 AM). Rush immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge — join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance, one of Disney's most immersive rides. Then ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run. Explore the incredible Star Wars land atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Toy Story Land for Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania. Then visit Sunset Boulevard for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror — two of Disney's most thrilling rides. Take a mid-afternoon break at the hotel if needed to avoid peak heat.
day_by_day.evening: Return for the evening to catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show times). End the night with Fantasmic! — a spectacular outdoor nighttime show featuring Mickey Mouse, Disney villains, and fireworks on the lagoon. Arrive 45–60 minutes early for good seating.

meals.breakfast: Hotel snacks — fruit, granola bars, and water from your Walmart supply
meals.lunch: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — fun theming with grilled cheese sandwiches and totchos (tater tot nachos) for around $10–$13 per person
meals.dinner: ABC Commissary near Echo Lake — burgers, wraps, and international dishes for around $12–$15 per person; one of the park's most affordable counter-service spots

day_by_day.notes: Hollywood Studios is the most ride-dense park — plan Lightning Lane Multi Pass for Rise of the Resistance if budget allows (around $20–$30 per person extra). Fantasmic! dining packages exist but are pricey — arrive early for free seating instead. Check the My Disney Experience app for live wait times throughout the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take the free hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom, arriving at rope drop (typically 8:00 AM — often opens earlier than other parks). Head straight to Pandora – The World of Avatar for Flight of Passage (the park's most popular ride — waits can exceed 2 hours by 9 AM). Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a beautiful, relaxing boat experience through bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Africa — take the Kilimanjaro Safaris for an incredible free-roaming animal experience (best in the morning or late afternoon when animals are most active — consider a second ride now). Walk the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail. Head to Asia for Expedition Everest and Kali River Rapids (you WILL get wet — great for the heat!).
day_by_day.evening: Catch the Rivers of Light nighttime spectacular if running (check schedule). Explore Discovery Island and the iconic Tree of Life — look for the hidden animal carvings. Animal Kingdom typically closes earlier than other parks, so head back to the hotel for a relaxing evening by the pool.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Zuri's Swamped Snacks near the park entrance — Mickey waffles or pastries for around $6–$8
meals.lunch: Flame Tree Barbecue in Discovery Island — one of Disney's best counter-service meals with smoked ribs, pulled pork, and chicken for around $14–$17 per person; beautiful outdoor waterfront seating
meals.dinner: Relax at the hotel — use your Walmart grocery supplies to make a simple meal in the room (sandwiches, fruit, chips) and save $30–$50 for the family. Or visit a nearby Kissimmee restaurant on W Irlo Bronson Hwy

day_by_day.notes: Animal Kingdom is best experienced in the morning — animals are more active and temperatures are cooler. Bring a change of clothes or a poncho for Kali River Rapids. The park often closes by 8–9 PM, making it the shortest park day — use the extra time to rest or explore the Kissimmee area near the hotel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely morning! Have a relaxed breakfast at the hotel. Spend the morning at the Ramada hotel pool — a great free activity to recharge after four intense park days. Let the kids splash around while you plan the final day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the free hotel shuttle (or a short rideshare — about $10–$15) to Disney Springs — Disney's free-admission shopping, dining, and entertainment district. Explore the World of Disney store (largest Disney merchandise store in the world), browse unique shops, watch street performers, and enjoy the lively atmosphere along the waterfront. Visit the LEGO Store with its impressive outdoor LEGO sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy dinner at Disney Springs and catch some live entertainment. Walk along the waterfront and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere. Head back to the hotel via shuttle or rideshare and pack for the final park day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Walmart snacks — fruit, yogurt, cereal to save money
meals.lunch: D-Luxe Burger at Disney Springs — gourmet burgers with creative toppings for around $13–$16 per person; great quality for the price
meals.dinner: Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza at Disney Springs — build-your-own personal pizzas for around $10–$13 per person; one of the best budget options at Disney Springs

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs admission is completely FREE — no park ticket required. This is a great budget day to rest legs and still enjoy Disney magic. The LEGO Store, World of Disney, and many other shops are free to browse. Avoid the sit-down restaurants at Disney Springs (The Boathouse, STK, etc.) as they are expensive — stick to counter service. Check for free live music performances on the waterfront stages.

day_by_day.morning: Final park day! Take the free hotel shuttle back to Magic Kingdom for a morning revisit. Use this day to ride anything you missed or loved from Day 2. Hit your favorite rides with shorter Sunday morning crowds. Grab a Mickey-shaped pretzel or Dole Whip as a classic Disney treat. Spend time on Main Street USA for last-minute souvenir shopping.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back to the hotel by early afternoon (around 1–2 PM). Check out of the hotel (or store luggage at the front desk). Take a final dip in the hotel pool. Pack all belongings and organize souvenirs. Arrange transportation back to Orlando International Airport — confirm hotel shuttle schedule or book a rideshare (Uber/Lyft typically $25–$35 to MCO).
day_by_day.evening: Head to Orlando International Airport for your departure flight. Arrive at least 2 hours before domestic departure or 3 hours for international. Reflect on an amazing week at Disney World! Browse airport shops for any last-minute Florida or Disney souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Casey's Corner on Main Street USA, Magic Kingdom — hot dogs and breakfast items for around $8–$11; a classic Disney quick-service spot
meals.lunch: Cosmic Ray's Starlight Café in Tomorrowland — one of Magic Kingdom's largest and most affordable counter-service restaurants with burgers, chicken, and rotisserie options for around $12–$15 per person
meals.dinner: Airport dining at MCO — grab a meal at one of the terminal restaurants or fast food options before your flight; budget around $12–$18 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time (usually 11 AM) — request a late checkout if your flight is in the evening. Use any remaining Disney gift cards or dining credits today. Take final photos at Magic Kingdom's iconic spots — Cinderella Castle, Main Street USA, and the park entrance. The free hotel shuttle to the airport may be available — confirm with the front desk the night before. Total estimated budget for 7 days (excluding flights and park tickets): $150–$250 per person for food using counter-service dining and Walmart grocery supplements.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Take the hotel's free theme park shuttle or a rideshare to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Grab a light snack from a nearby 24-hour convenience store or the hotel vending area before getting a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport before departure.
meals.lunch: On the plane or at the airport.
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from hotel vending, a nearby 7-Eleven, or a quick drive-through such as McDonald's or Taco Bell on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy (open late).

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 extremely light. Hydrate well after the flight. Set alarms early for Day 2 to maximize park time. Confirm shuttle schedule with the front desk upon check-in. June in Orlando is hot and humid with afternoon thunderstorms common — pack sunscreen, ponchos, and refillable water bottles for the week.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park – Arrive at rope drop (park typically opens at 9:00 AM; aim to board the free hotel shuttle by 7:45 AM to arrive early). Start with the most popular rides before crowds build: Space Mountain, Big Thunder Mountain Railroad, and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train. Use Disney's Lightning Lane or Virtual Queue options where available. Grab a Mickey-shaped pretzel or breakfast pastry from a Main Street bakery cart.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Magic Kingdom. Ride Pirates of the Caribbean, the Haunted Mansion, and It's a Small World. Watch the Festival of Fantasy parade (typically early afternoon). Take a mid-afternoon break in an air-conditioned attraction or the Tomorrowland Terrace to escape the peak heat (usually 1:00–3:00 PM). Enjoy a Dole Whip at Aloha Isle for a classic Disney treat.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Magic Kingdom nighttime spectacular — the iconic 'Disney Enchantment' fireworks show over Cinderella Castle (check the park schedule for exact time, usually 9:00 PM). Grab a prime viewing spot on Main Street U.S.A. at least 30 minutes early. Return to the hotel via the free shuttle after the show.

meals.breakfast: Quick-service pastries and coffee at Main Street Bakery (Starbucks-affiliated) inside Magic Kingdom — budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House in Liberty Square — excellent mid-range quick-service with clam chowder, fish and chips, and chicken sandwiches. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Be Our Guest Restaurant in Fantasyland (book in advance via the My Disney Experience app) for a mid-range table-service dinner inside the Beast's Castle. Budget ~$25–$40 per person. Alternatively, Tony's Town Square Restaurant on Main Street for a more casual Italian option.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Disney park tickets and make dining reservations well in advance (60 days out for table-service). Download the My Disney Experience app for real-time wait times and Lightning Lane purchases. Wear comfortable, closed-toe shoes. Bring a small backpack with sunscreen, a poncho, and a portable phone charger.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios & Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure – Board the hotel shuttle early to arrive at park opening (typically 9:00 AM). Head straight to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge. Ride Millennium Falcon: Smugglers Run first (shorter morning wait), then join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance, one of the most immersive theme park experiences ever built. Explore the land, interact with droids, and visit Savi's Workshop to build a custom lightsaber (extra cost, ~$249.99 — optional splurge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios. Ride Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania in Toy Story Land. Visit the Tower of Terror and Rock 'n' Roller Coaster for thrill seekers. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular (check show schedule). Take a short break during peak afternoon heat with a cold treat from Woody's Lunch Box.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Hollywood Studios nighttime show — 'Fantasmic!' (check schedule, usually 8:00 or 9:00 PM), a spectacular water, fire, and projection show. Arrive 45 minutes early for good seats. Return to the hotel via shuttle after the show.

meals.breakfast: Woody's Lunch Box in Toy Story Land — try the Lunch Box Tarts and a Raspberry Lemonade. Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo inside Galaxy's Edge — themed quick-service with dishes like Smoked Kaadu Ribs and Fried Endorian Tip-Yip. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant — a unique mid-range table-service experience where you eat in retro cars watching classic sci-fi movie clips. Book in advance. Budget ~$20–$35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rise of the Resistance is extremely popular — check the My Disney Experience app the moment the park opens to secure a Lightning Lane or boarding group. Savi's Workshop lightsaber building requires a reservation and is an additional cost but is a memorable family experience. Fantasmic! seating fills up fast — consider the Fantasmic! Dining Package for reserved seating.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Arrive at EPCOT at opening (typically 9:00 AM). Start in Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature) and ride Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue — join immediately at park open) and Test Track. Visit the stunning Spaceship Earth geodesic sphere. Head to World Showcase when it opens at 11:00 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon exploring EPCOT's World Showcase — a living cultural journey through 11 country pavilions including Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample food and drinks from each pavilion (this is the heart of the EPCOT experience). Ride Frozen Ever After in the Norway Pavilion and Remy's Ratatouille Adventure in the France Pavilion (Lightning Lane recommended). Browse unique international merchandise and watch cultural performances.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for EPCOT's 'EPCOT Forever' or 'Harmonious' nighttime spectacular over World Showcase Lagoon (check current show schedule — one of the largest nighttime shows Disney has ever created). Watch from the World Showcase promenade. Return to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons in The Land pavilion — fresh, affordable quick-service with sandwiches, salads, and hot breakfast items. Budget ~$12–$18 per person.
meals.lunch: World Showcase food stalls — graze through multiple countries. Try a School Bread from Norway (~$6), a crepe from France (~$8), and a Kakigori shaved ice from Japan (~$7). Budget ~$20–$30 per person total for a tasting experience.
meals.dinner: Teppan Edo in the Japan Pavilion — a lively mid-range teppanyaki table-service restaurant. Book well in advance. Budget ~$30–$45 per person. Alternatively, La Hacienda de San Angel in the Mexico Pavilion for waterfront dining with lagoon views.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT is the most 'adult-friendly' Disney park but kids love Frozen Ever After and Remy's Ratatouille Adventure. The World Showcase is perfect for foodies — budget extra for food and drink tastings. If visiting during a festival (EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival runs summer through fall), there will be additional food booths and entertainment throughout the park — a major highlight.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom Expedition & Pandora Experience – Arrive at park opening (typically 8:00 AM — Animal Kingdom often has early entry). Head immediately to Pandora – The World of Avatar. Ride Avatar Flight of Passage first (the most popular ride in the park — waits can exceed 2 hours by mid-morning). The bioluminescent landscape of Pandora is breathtaking. Then ride Na'vi River Journey for a gentler, visually stunning experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Animal Kingdom. Take the Kilimanjaro Safaris for a genuine wildlife experience (morning and late afternoon are best for animal activity — consider a second ride). Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close animal encounters. Ride Expedition Everest in Asia for a thrilling roller coaster. Watch the Festival of the Lion King show (check schedule) — one of Disney's best live performances.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the Rivers of Light nighttime show at Animal Kingdom (check if currently running — schedules vary). Alternatively, head to Disney Springs for a relaxed evening of shopping, dining, and free entertainment (no park ticket required). Return to the hotel via shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick bite at Zuri's Swamped Snacks near the park entrance — try the Mickey waffles or a breakfast sandwich. Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Satu'li Canteen in Pandora — the best quick-service restaurant in Animal Kingdom with healthy, flavorful bowls and unique beverages. Try the Cheeseburger Steamed Pods or a Blueberry Cream Cheese Mousse. Budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Yak & Yeti Restaurant in Asia — a mid-range table-service restaurant with Asian fusion cuisine in a beautifully themed setting. Book in advance. Budget ~$20–$35 per person. Or head to Disney Springs for dinner at The BOATHOUSE or Raglan Road Irish Pub.

day_by_day.notes: Avatar Flight of Passage is a must-do but has very high demand — use Lightning Lane if available or arrive at rope drop. Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (often by 8:00–9:00 PM), so plan accordingly. The park is very walkable but large — wear comfortable shoes. June heat is intense here with less shade than other parks — stay hydrated and take breaks.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and Resort Morning – Take a well-deserved slower morning. Sleep in, enjoy a leisurely breakfast, and relax by the hotel pool. This is a great recovery day mid-trip, especially important for families with children. Use the morning to recharge, do laundry if needed, and review plans for the final days. Alternatively, use this morning to revisit a favorite park for any missed attractions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment – Head to Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required) via the hotel shuttle or rideshare. Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Browse unique Disney merchandise at World of Disney (the largest Disney store on Earth). Visit the LEGO Store, check out the NBA Experience, or catch a movie at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Browse art galleries and unique boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a full Disney Springs entertainment evening. Watch street performers and live music acts throughout the complex. Visit Splitsville Luxury Lanes for bowling and entertainment (great for families). Browse the shops as they stay open late. Enjoy the waterfront atmosphere along the lake.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby IHOP/Denny's on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy for a classic American breakfast. Budget ~$10–$15 per person.
meals.lunch: Blaze Fast-Fire'd Pizza at Disney Springs — build-your-own artisan pizza at a great mid-range price. Budget ~$12–$16 per person.
meals.dinner: The BOATHOUSE at Disney Springs — a mid-range to upscale waterfront restaurant with excellent seafood, steaks, and a stunning fleet of vintage amphicars. Budget ~$35–$55 per person. Alternatively, Raglan Road Irish Pub for a livelier atmosphere with live Irish music, dancing, and hearty pub fare at ~$20–$35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great way to experience Disney magic without a park ticket. Parking is also free in the Disney Springs garages. Saturday is typically the busiest day at Disney Springs — arrive early for dinner reservations or book well in advance. The Amphicar tours at The BOATHOUSE are a unique paid experience (~$125 for 20 minutes) — a fun family splurge.

day_by_day.morning: Return to a Favorite Park or Flex Day – Use this final full day to revisit your favorite park, catch any missed attractions, or explore something new. Recommended: Return to Magic Kingdom for any rides missed on Day 2, or revisit EPCOT for more World Showcase exploration. Alternatively, if the family wants a water park day, Disney's Typhoon Lagoon or Blizzard Beach are excellent options (separate ticket required, ~$79–$99 per person) — perfect for a hot June day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final park exploration or resort relaxation. If departing the next day, use the afternoon to begin packing, do any final souvenir shopping at the park or Disney Springs, and enjoy a last leisurely stroll through your favorite Disney area. Take photos at iconic spots — Cinderella Castle, the EPCOT geodesic sphere, or the Tree of Life at Animal Kingdom.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner – Celebrate the end of a magical trip with a special dinner. Head back to the hotel for an early evening, pack remaining items, confirm transportation for departure, and get a good night's rest. Reflect on the week's highlights and memories made.

meals.breakfast: Quick hotel breakfast or a grab-and-go option from a nearby Publix or Wawa convenience store on W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy. Budget ~$8–$12 per person.
meals.lunch: Park quick-service of choice based on which park you visit — budget ~$15–$20 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebration dinner at Olivia's Café at Disney's Old Key West Resort (accessible via Disney transportation) for a relaxed, mid-range Florida Keys-themed dinner. Budget ~$25–$40 per person. Or return to a Disney Springs favorite for a final memorable meal.

day_by_day.notes: If your return flight is on June 22, confirm the flight time and arrange transportation the night before. The hotel's free theme park shuttle may not run to the airport — book a rideshare (Uber/Lyft) or Mears Connect shuttle in advance for airport transfers (~$16–$25 per person one-way). Leave extra time for Orlando International Airport security, especially in summer. Don't forget to check all hotel rooms for left-behind items before checkout.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Disney World, Orlando, Florida Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway - Free Theme Park Shuttle
hotel.location: 7470 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, US (28.3314,-81.5863)

experiences.name: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day
experiences.description: Spend a full day at the iconic Magic Kingdom, home to Cinderella Castle, Space Mountain, and the beloved Festival of Fantasy parade. Arrive at rope drop (park opening) to maximize ride time before crowds build. With a late flight arrival on Day 1, plan this for Day 2 onward. Stay at a Disney on-site hotel like Disney's Contemporary Resort or Disney's Polynesian Village Resort — both are within walking distance or a short monorail ride to Magic Kingdom, eliminating transit time and letting you return for afternoon naps before evening fireworks.
experiences.location: Magic Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour
experiences.description: Explore EPCOT's World Showcase, a living cultural and culinary journey through 11 countries including Mexico, Japan, France, and Morocco. Sample authentic dishes, watch live cultural performances, and browse artisan crafts. This is ideal for families who want entertainment and education combined. Stay at Disney's BoardWalk Inn or Disney's Beach Club Resort — both are within a short walk or boat ride to EPCOT's International Gateway entrance, saving significant travel time each day.
experiences.location: EPCOT, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Hollywood Studios & Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure
experiences.description: Immerse your family in the fully realized world of Star Wars at Galaxy's Edge, where you can pilot the Millennium Falcon, build a custom lightsaber, and encounter stormtroopers. Also enjoy Toy Story Land and the thrilling Tower of Terror. Book Lightning Lane passes in advance for top attractions. Disney's Art of Animation Resort and Disney's Pop Century Resort are directly connected to Hollywood Studios via the Disney Skyliner gondola system — a fun, fast, and free transit option that kids love.
experiences.location: Hollywood Studios, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment Evening
experiences.description: Spend a relaxed evening at Disney Springs, Disney's free-admission shopping, dining, and entertainment district. Enjoy dinner at The BOATHOUSE or Rainforest Cafe, catch a live street performance, and browse Disney merchandise and unique shops. This is a perfect low-cost activity for Day 1 since your flight arrives after 20:00 — Disney Springs stays open until 11:00 PM and requires no park ticket. It's a great way to ease into the Disney experience without wasting a full park day.
experiences.location: Disney Springs, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

experiences.name: Disney's Animal Kingdom Expedition & Pandora Experience
experiences.description: Explore Disney's Animal Kingdom, featuring the breathtaking Pandora – The World of Avatar with the Flight of Passage ride, a thrilling safari through Kilimanjaro Safaris, and live shows like Festival of the Lion King. This park is best experienced starting at morning rope drop when animals are most active. Disney's All-Star Resorts and Disney's Coronado Springs Resort offer affordable on-site stays with direct Disney bus service to Animal Kingdom, keeping your family close to the action throughout the week.
experiences.location: Animal Kingdom, Walt Disney World Resort, Lake Buena Vista

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight UA arrives at 22:30. No morning or afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Orlando International Airport at 22:30. Take the hotel's complimentary theme park shuttle or a pre-arranged private car transfer to Ramada by Wyndham Kissimmee Gateway. Check in, unpack, and settle into your room. Order a late-night room service spread or grab a quick premium bite at a nearby 24-hour spot to wind down after travel.

meals.breakfast: In-flight or at the airport before departure
meals.lunch: In-flight or at the airport
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at the hotel or a quick stop at a nearby restaurant such as Perkins Restaurant & Bakery (open late, ~5 min drive) for a relaxed post-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury car or town car service from Orlando International Airport for a seamless, stress-free arrival. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is after 10 PM. Lay out park bags and essentials tonight so Day 2 starts smoothly. Purchase Disney park tickets and make Lightning Lane Multi Pass reservations in advance via the My Disney Experience app.

day_by_day.morning: Magic Kingdom Park Full Day – Begin with an early rope-drop entry (park opens at 9:00 AM; arrive by 8:30 AM via the hotel's free theme park shuttle). Head straight to Tomorrowland for Space Mountain using Lightning Lane, then tackle TRON Lightcycle / Run and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train before crowds build. Explore Fantasyland and meet characters at Princess Fairytale Hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue your Magic Kingdom adventure through the afternoon. Experience Pirates of the Caribbean, Haunted Mansion, and Big Thunder Mountain Railroad. Catch the Festival of Fantasy Parade (typically 3:00 PM) from a premium viewing spot near Main Street U.S.A. Take a mid-afternoon break at a shaded area or the hotel for a quick rest if needed.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Magic Kingdom for the spectacular EPCOT Forever or Magic Kingdom's Happily Ever After fireworks spectacular (check current show schedule). Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Main Street U.S.A. illuminated at night before heading back to the hotel via the shuttle.

meals.breakfast: Be Our Guest Restaurant (Magic Kingdom) – Premium table-service breakfast inside the Beast's enchanted castle; book well in advance via My Disney Experience
meals.lunch: Columbia Harbour House or Skipper Canteen – Skipper Canteen offers a unique, story-rich table-service lunch experience with globally inspired cuisine
meals.dinner: Cinderella's Royal Table – Iconic fine-dining inside Cinderella Castle with princess character meet-and-greets; one of Disney's most coveted reservations (book 60 days in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Lightning Lane Individual Attraction selections for TRON Lightcycle / Run and Seven Dwarfs Mine Train as early as 7:00 AM on the day of your visit. Wear comfortable, breathable clothing as June in Orlando is hot and humid (expect 90°F+). Stay hydrated and use Disney's complimentary water cup stations. The hotel shuttle schedule should be confirmed the night before.

day_by_day.morning: Hollywood Studios & Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge Adventure – Take the hotel shuttle to Disney's Hollywood Studios for rope-drop (arrive by 8:30 AM). Head immediately to Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge and join the virtual queue or Lightning Lane for Rise of the Resistance, one of Disney's most immersive and technologically advanced attractions. Then pilot the Millennium Falcon on Smugglers Run.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Hollywood Studios: experience Slinky Dog Dash and Toy Story Mania in Toy Story Land, then head to Sunset Boulevard for Rock 'n' Roller Coaster Starring Aerosmith and The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Catch the Indiana Jones Epic Stunt Spectacular show (check schedule). Take a mid-afternoon break with a cool treat at Woody's Lunch Box.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the breathtaking Fantasmic! nighttime spectacular at the Hollywood Hills Amphitheater (check current schedule). For a premium experience, book the Fantasmic! Dining Package at a Hollywood Studios restaurant, which includes reserved Fantasmic! seating. End the night with a stroll through Galaxy's Edge lit up beautifully after dark.

meals.breakfast: Docking Bay 7 Food and Cargo (Galaxy's Edge) – Immersive Star Wars-themed quick-service with unique, creative dishes; grab a Ronto Wrap and Blue or Green Milk for the full experience
meals.lunch: Sci-Fi Dine-In Theater Restaurant – Unique table-service dining inside a retro drive-in movie theater showing classic sci-fi clips; a Hollywood Studios signature experience
meals.dinner: Hollywood Brown Derby – Hollywood Studios' premier fine-dining restaurant inspired by the legendary 1930s Hollywood landmark; known for the Cobb Salad and exceptional service. Book the Fantasmic! Dining Package here for reserved show seating.

day_by_day.notes: Rise of the Resistance is extremely popular – secure a Lightning Lane Individual Attraction pass at exactly 7:00 AM via the My Disney Experience app. The Fantasmic! Dining Package must be booked in advance and includes a voucher for reserved seating. June heat peaks in the afternoon (2–4 PM); plan a short hotel break or use air-conditioned attractions during peak heat hours.

day_by_day.morning: EPCOT World Showcase Food & Culture Tour – Arrive at EPCOT at rope-drop (9:00 AM). Begin in Future World (now called World Discovery and World Nature) and experience Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind (virtual queue or Lightning Lane) and Test Track. Then head to Soarin' Around the World for a breathtaking aerial journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transition into the World Showcase as it opens at 11:00 AM. Embark on a self-guided premium food and culture tour through all 11 country pavilions – Mexico, Norway, China, Germany, Italy, America, Japan, Morocco, France, United Kingdom, and Canada. Sample signature dishes and beverages at each pavilion. Highlights include the Norway pavilion's Frozen Ever After ride and the France pavilion's Remy's Ratatouille Adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Conclude your World Showcase tour and find a premium viewing spot along World Showcase Lagoon for EPCOT's stunning nighttime spectacular (EPCOT Forever or Luminous the Symphony of Us – confirm current show). Enjoy the fireworks and projection show over the lagoon before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Sunshine Seasons (EPCOT's Land Pavilion) – Fresh, high-quality quick-service breakfast with healthy options; or grab a pastry at the France Pavilion's Les Halles Boulangerie-Patisserie
meals.lunch: Teppan Edo (Japan Pavilion) – Premium teppanyaki-style table-service dining with skilled chefs cooking at your table; a theatrical and delicious experience
meals.dinner: Monsieur Paul (France Pavilion) – EPCOT's most upscale fine-dining restaurant, a French haute cuisine experience inspired by legendary chef Paul Bocuse; exceptional wine list and impeccable service. Reservations essential 60 days in advance.

day_by_day.notes: EPCOT's World Showcase is a food lover's paradise – budget extra for food and beverage tastings across pavilions (approximately $15–$30 per stop). The EPCOT International Food & Wine Festival may be running in June – check Disney's event calendar for bonus food booths and special programming. Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind requires a virtual queue or Lightning Lane Individual Attraction – secure it at 7:00 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Disney's Animal Kingdom Expedition & Pandora Experience – Take the hotel shuttle to Animal Kingdom for rope-drop (8:00 AM). Head directly to Pandora – The World of Avatar and experience Avatar Flight of Passage, the park's most thrilling and visually stunning ride (Lightning Lane Individual Attraction recommended). Then experience Na'vi River Journey for a serene, beautifully crafted boat ride through bioluminescent rainforest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rest of Animal Kingdom: embark on Kilimanjaro Safaris for an authentic African savanna experience with live animals (morning or early afternoon is best for animal activity). Visit the Gorilla Falls Exploration Trail and Maharajah Jungle Trek for up-close wildlife encounters. Experience Expedition Everest – Legend of the Forbidden Mountain in Asia and DINOSAUR in DinoLand U.S.A.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for Animal Kingdom's magical evening transformation. Experience Rivers of Light: We Are One nighttime spectacular (confirm current schedule) or enjoy Pandora at night when the bioluminescent landscape glows brilliantly. This is one of Disney's most visually stunning after-dark experiences. Return to the hotel for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Satu'li Canteen (Pandora) – The park's best quick-service option with creative, healthy bowls and unique Pandoran-themed dishes; arrive early to beat lines
meals.lunch: Tiffins Restaurant – Animal Kingdom's premier fine-dining table-service restaurant with globally inspired cuisine, stunning artwork, and an exceptional wine and cocktail program; a true hidden gem
meals.dinner: Nomad Lounge (adjacent to Tiffins) – Enjoy premium cocktails, small plates, and shared dishes in a beautifully designed lounge atmosphere; perfect for a relaxed, upscale evening wind-down before heading back to the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Avatar Flight of Passage is the single most in-demand attraction at Walt Disney World – secure a Lightning Lane Individual Attraction pass at 7:00 AM sharp. Kilimanjaro Safaris is best experienced in the morning or late afternoon when animals are most active. Animal Kingdom closes earlier than other parks (typically 8–9 PM) – check the current park hours. Pandora at night is a must-see; plan to be there as the sun sets.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed Morning & Resort Experience – Take a well-deserved late start. Enjoy a leisurely premium breakfast at the hotel or a nearby upscale restaurant. Use the morning to relax by the hotel pool, do some souvenir shopping, or explore the Kissimmee area. Optionally, visit Disney Springs for morning shopping at luxury boutiques including the World of Disney store, LEGO Store, and Uniqlo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disney Springs Dining & Entertainment – Spend the afternoon at Disney Springs (free admission, no park ticket required). Explore the four neighborhoods: The Landing, Marketplace, Town Center, and West Side. Browse premium shops, visit the NBA Experience, or catch a show at the AMC Disney Springs 24 theater. Enjoy the vibrant waterfront atmosphere along Lake Buena Vista.
day_by_day.evening: Disney Springs Evening Entertainment Extravaganza – Experience the full Disney Springs evening atmosphere with live entertainment, street performers, and the iconic Aerophile balloon ride for panoramic views of the Walt Disney World Resort. Enjoy a premium dinner at one of Disney Springs' signature restaurants before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: The Polite Pig (Disney Springs) or a hotel breakfast – Alternatively, visit Amorette's Patisserie at Disney Springs for exquisite pastries and coffee as a late morning treat
meals.lunch: Wine Bar George – Disney Springs' premier wine bar and restaurant featuring an award-winning wine list, charcuterie boards, and elevated small plates; a sophisticated midday experience
meals.dinner: Morimoto Asia – Celebrity chef Masaharu Morimoto's flagship pan-Asian restaurant at Disney Springs; stunning two-story space with exceptional sushi, dim sum, and Asian-fusion cuisine. One of the finest dining experiences in all of Orlando.

day_by_day.notes: Disney Springs is free to enter and a great way to enjoy a Disney atmosphere without a park ticket. The Aerophile tethered balloon ride offers spectacular sunset views and is a unique premium experience (~$25 per person). Saturday evenings at Disney Springs are very lively – expect larger crowds. Make dinner reservations at Morimoto Asia well in advance. This is also a great day to purchase any remaining souvenirs or gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Magic Kingdom or EPCOT for Final Park Day – Choose your favorite park for one last magical morning. If returning to Magic Kingdom, focus on any attractions missed earlier and enjoy a final stroll down Main Street U.S.A. If choosing EPCOT, revisit favorite World Showcase pavilions and pick up any last international souvenirs or specialty food items.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Afternoon at the Park – Spend the afternoon enjoying your chosen park at a relaxed, unhurried pace. Revisit favorite rides, take photos at iconic landmarks (Cinderella Castle, Spaceship Earth), and soak in the final moments of your Disney World experience. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at the park's premium gift shops.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Dinner & Hotel Return – Enjoy a special farewell dinner at a premium restaurant near the hotel or at Disney Springs. Return to the hotel, pack, and prepare for departure. Reflect on an incredible week of Disney magic with your family.

meals.breakfast: Crystal Palace (Magic Kingdom) – Elegant Victorian-style buffet breakfast with Winnie the Pooh and friends character meet-and-greet; a warm, memorable final Disney breakfast experience
meals.lunch: Liberty Tree Tavern (Magic Kingdom) or Coral Reef Restaurant (EPCOT) – Liberty Tree Tavern offers hearty American fare in a colonial setting; Coral Reef features stunning floor-to-ceiling aquarium views with fresh seafood
meals.dinner: The Ravenous Pig or Christner's Prime Steak & Lobster (Kissimmee/Orlando area) – For a farewell dinner near the hotel, Christner's Prime Steak & Lobster is a classic Orlando fine-dining institution with USDA prime steaks, fresh lobster, and an extensive wine cellar; perfect for a celebratory final evening

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is on June 22 or later, this final evening is perfect for a relaxed, celebratory dinner. Confirm hotel checkout time and arrange transportation to Orlando International Airport in advance – book a private luxury car or town car for a premium, stress-free departure. Download all Disney PhotoPass photos from My Disney Experience before leaving (or purchase Memory Maker in advance to capture all professional park photos). Allow extra time for packing souvenirs and gifts.
